title: Morning Brief — Thu 26 Nov

stories.board: Judges cast doubt on Netanyahu's biggest charge
stories.headline: Big boost for Netanyahu in his corruption trial
stories.what: Israeli judges said a conviction (being found guilty) in Case 4000, the most serious case, looks unlikely. They asked prosecutors to rethink another case and to try to make a deal on the third.
stories.why: The trial has gone on since 2020, and it shapes who can lead Israel. Nothing has been dropped yet.
stories.sides: Netanyahu and right-leaning outlets say the trial fell apart; others stress the judges' words were only advice, not a verdict (final decision).

stories.board: Storm brings heavy rain, ice to southern Ontario
stories.headline: Wet, windy and icy Thanksgiving Thursday in Ontario
stories.what: Weather warnings are out for southern Ontario. Heavy rain and wind gusts near 60 km/h are expected, and some areas could get freezing rain (rain that turns to ice) by Friday morning.
stories.why: Roads and sidewalks may be slippery and power could go out in spots.

stories.board: US probes Iran link to hacks on ships
stories.headline: US looks into hacking of up to 50 ships
stories.what: The US government is checking whether Iran is behind cyberattacks (computer break-ins) on as many as 50 commercial ships. Iran also says more tankers hit sea mines near the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route.
stories.why: A lot of the world's oil passes there, so trouble can raise fuel prices.
stories.sides: No major disagreement; Iran's mine claims have not been confirmed by others.

quick_hits: Israel's Gadi Eisenkot wants deals with Bennett and Golan by Saturday so a new government can start next week (Ynetnews).
Storms and crowds are causing flight delays on American Thanksgiving; US stock markets are closed today.
Bank of Canada boss Tiff Macklem warned that past jumps in energy prices could still push prices up.
big_picture: Netanyahu got good news in court while his rivals race to replace him, and here at home it is a stormy day.
